before_step.derivation: Given a fixed job order J1,...,Jn and the setup times s_i from step 1, let C_0 = 0 (prior completion before any job). For each k in order: setup can begin only after both the job's release r_{Jk} and the prior completion C_{k-1}, so the setup start is T_k = max(r_{Jk}, C_{k-1}). Setup time is s_k (initial s_1 = index(J1) mod 3; otherwise s_k = abs(index(J_{k-1})-index(J_k)) mod 3). Hence the processing start is P_k = T_k + s_k, and because the machine is nonpreemptive the completion is C_k = P_k + p_{Jk}, where p is the job's processing time. Equivalently C_k = max(r_{Jk}, C_{k-1}) + s_k + p_{Jk}. Since setup may only begin after release, T_k is a true lower bound of the earliest feasible setup start; no idle beyond that is needed because inserting extra idle cannot reduce any C_k. This recurrence is purely definitional from the givens and step 1; it selects no order and identifies no optimum.
before_step.result: For order J1..Jn: T_k = max(r_{Jk}, C_{k-1}), s_1 = index(J1) mod 3, s_k = abs(index(J_{k-1})-index(J_k)) mod 3 (k>1), P_k = T_k + s_k, C_k = P_k + p_{Jk}, with C_0 = 0. Equivalently C_k = max(r_{Jk}, C_{k-1}) + s_k + p_{Jk}.

plan_step.goal: For any fixed job order, define recurrence for setup start, processing start, and completion using release times and prior completion.
